paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Wisdom beats folly the way light beats darkness, and the Teacher says so himself (Ecclesiastes 2:13). But he also sees that "one fate overcomes them both," and even the wise man is forgotten (Ecclesiastes 2:14, 16). Being wise won't save you, and neither will a pile of labor, because it all gets handed to somebody else (Ecclesiastes 2:18).

So what do you do with that? The Teacher doesn't tell you to quit. He says "Nothing is better for a man than to eat and drink and enjoy his work," and that this "is from the hand of God" (Ecclesiastes 2:24). Then he asks, "For apart from Him, who can eat and who can find enjoyment?" (Ecclesiastes 2:25). Chasing success is like chasing wind, but enjoying your work as a gift from God is something you can actually hold.

I know a little about this, friend, because I lost my joy in the dark and the Most High is the One who gave it back. Today, let your work be a gift you receive instead of a prize you have to win. Do it with thanks, and leave the rest in the hands of the One who gives "wisdom and knowledge and joy" (Ecclesiastes 2:26). Now THAT is a batch worth baking!
